text:
Joel Eriksson Ek is the Wild's two-way centre, and Matt Boldy went public this month saying he doesn't get the credit he deserves. Our numbers partly agree, because two kinds of luck are running through his season in opposite directions.

His own shots are unlucky: 10 goals on 13.4 expected. He keeps getting to the net, and goals tend to follow chances. But Minnesota has scored 11.3 more goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, and that is padding his 26 points. Net it out and you have a player whose underlying game is better than ever: the Wild take 58% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, 7.6 points better than without him, and his point rate (3.12 per 60) sits above his talent range. He throws hits (33) and blocks shots, and he centres a line Michael Russo has been praising for weeks. Our range projects 58 to 80 points. Watch the goal column: it should rise while the on-ice luck fades.
